subject: Interim recovery plan and customer playbook — GPU pool degradation (us-west-2)
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Bhatia <sam@oliveai.com>, Alicia Gomez <it-ops@acme-corp.com>
Cc: dev@redwood.ai, marissa@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 25 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Interim recovery plan and customer playbook — GPU pool degradation (us-west-2)

Hi Samir / Alicia,

Thank you for your patience — I wanted to send a concise update and an interim plan while our engineers finish the deeper analysis. Summary up front: we observed sustained throughput degradation on the dedicated GPU pool serving OliveAI (us-west-2) starting ~2026-07-25 06:40 PDT. Impact: elevated tail latency and throttled batch throughput for your reserved nodes; some jobs experienced 30-60% slower token throughput.

What we're doing now (executive summary):
- Routing: we’ve enabled emergency routing to a warm failover pool in a different rack within the same region to restore steady throughput for non-latency-sensitive batches.
- Throttle policies: temporarily relaxed autoscaler thresholds to reduce pod churn and stabilize KV cache hot-keys.
- Mitigation work: infra team is collecting kernel traces and GPU telemetry to identify contention caused by a recent autoscaler change.

Immediate customer playbook (actions you can take):
1) For critical latency-sensitive endpoints, change the model routing to the fallback model variant we provisioned (model-id: redwood-gpt-small-fallback). This will restore p95 latency within ~2–3s for most calls.
2) For batch jobs, allow the job scheduler to hit the warm failover pool (no action required if you use our dedicated routing flags).
3) If you’d like us to initiate a short maintenance window to apply safe kernel/workload patches, reply with preferred windows and we’ll align.

I’ve attached an interim_recovery_plan.pdf with a brief timeline and suggested rollback criteria. Dev (dev_patel) is on the thread and will share a technical snapshot next.

Sorry for the disruption. We know predictable throughput is critical and we’ll keep you informed with hourly updates until we transition to a full postmortem.

— Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
irene@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0124

Subject: Re: Interim recovery plan and customer playbook — GPU pool degradation (us-west-2)

Irene — thanks for the fast update. Confirming we saw increased tail latency and a few queued jobs failing to start earlier this morning. A couple quick questions:

- Can you confirm whether the warm failover pool uses the same quantization/profile as our reserved pool? We have strict output parity requirements.
- If we switch critical endpoints to redwood-gpt-small-fallback, should we expect any differences in logits or tokenization? Our validation is strict for customer-facing flows.

Prefer a maintenance window tomorrow 07/26 between 0200–0400 PDT if that helps. Also please advise on how credits or billing adjustments will be handled for the degraded period — we may escalate renewals if this persists.

Samir Bhatia
Head of Platform Engineering, OliveAI
sam@oliveai.com
From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>, Samir Bhatia <sam@oliveai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 25 Jul 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Interim recovery plan and customer playbook — GPU pool degradation (us-west-2)

Hi all — quick technical snapshot from infra: we’ve reproduced the degradation in staging and confirmed a behavioral change introduced by the autoscaler v2.4.1 rollout earlier this week. Root observations:
- Autoscaler aggressively consolidated low-utilization processes causing hot-cache eviction on a subset of dedicated nodes; this increased repeated KV cache misses during token generation and amplified GPU kernel contention.
- Failure mode appears when working set > 12M KV entries and sequence lengths > 1,024 concurrently.

Immediate actions taken (done):
- Rolled back autoscaler to v2.4.0 on dedicated pools to stop consolidation churn.
- Enabled conservative cache pinning for OliveAI’s node group to keep hot KV in memory.
- Flushed and collected kernel traces; attaching cluster-logs-2026-07-25.zip for deep trace (sensitive).

Planned next steps (24–72 hours):
- Analyze kernel traces with vendor HAL to confirm whether cache eviction is driver-level or scheduling-level.
- If driver-level, we will coordinate a micro-patch and schedule a maintenance window (we propose the time Samir suggested: 2026-07-26 02:00–04:00 PDT).
- If scheduling-level, we will deploy a tuning patch to the autoscaler with a canary rollout to dedicated pools.

Answers to Samir’s questions: the warm failover pool uses identical model quantization/profile by default; the fallback model is a trimmed variant but tokenization and logits are preserved — small probability-mass differences possible on marginal tokens. We will provide a short A/B eval for your team to validate parity.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: cluster-logs-2026-07-25.zip (12MB, logs + traces)
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Interim recovery plan and customer playbook — GPU pool degradation (us-west-2)

Samir — thanks for the questions and for the proposed window. Next steps and ask list:

1) Maintenance window confirmed: 2026-07-26 02:00–04:00 PDT. We will do a short kernel/workload patch during that window and keep the rollback criteria in the attached interim_recovery_plan.pdf. Please confirm if that window works for you.

2) Credit/billing: our billing team has provisionally scoped a credit for the sustained degradation period. Marissa (cc’d) will own the formal credit calculation and procurement conversation; she will follow up with a one-off billing adjustment proposal by EOD 2026-07-27.

3) Parity validation: we’ll provide an A/B payload sample and a short eval report within 4 hours of routing to the fallback model so your team can validate token-level parity.

4) Postmortem cadence: we plan an internal RCA and then a customer-facing postmortem doc within 7 business days. We’ll share a public summary and a confidential technical appendix with kernel traces.

Quoted below is Dev’s technical snapshot for reference.

Irene / team — confirming the maintenance window works for OliveAI. We initiated the fallback routing this morning (non-prod first) and results look promising — p95 is back in range for the evaluated endpoints. Please proceed with the maintenance during the confirmed window and send the A/B payload as soon as available.

On credits: we’d like a formal proposal from your billing team. If possible, include an estimate for lost throughput for the period 2026-07-25 06:40 PDT through 2026-07-25 14:15 PDT (our monitoring shows that as the window of greatest impact). We’ll route billing questions to Marissa when she sends the proposal.

Thanks for the transparency and the fast triage. Looking forward to the postmortem and the technical appendix.

— Samir
